The base-verb phrase attaches grammatically to 'allowed to' with no seam defects.

perOption.label: ④

perOption.label: ⑤

It also misstates the sign's true meaning (no parking/waiting, not no decelerating — the friend explicitly says cars may stop to pick up passengers), so it matches neither Carol's belief nor the correct interpretation.

note: Clean single-answer item. All five options are syntactically valid complements of 'allowed to', so discrimination is purely semantic/logical. The friend's direct rebuttal ('Of course you can stand there') uniquely selects ③ as the negated proposition; ③'s wording is a deliberate stilted paraphrase of 'stand' to avoid lexical echo, which is acceptable. ⑤ is the strongest distractor but is ruled out because it swaps Carol's mistaken belief for (an inaccurate version of) the sign's real meaning. No alternative parse or construal renders any other option defensible.
